source_name: Assembly of Kosovo — draft laws and committee pages (media-hearing anchor)
why_relevant: Pointer that lets media reports about parliamentary hearings and draft-law stages be resolved to the actual legislative file and deadline; also names the committee (Economy) whose sessions the Albanian press covers.

source_name: Office of the Prime Minister — concept documents and draft laws (media follow-through anchor)
why_relevant: Media reports of cabinet approvals point here for the actual text — e.g. the Draft Law on Payment Services PDF and the Concept Document on developing the regulatory framework for financial markets, which is where quiet consultations originate.

source_name: Zëri.info
why_relevant: Long-established Kosovo daily with an economy desk; a redundancy source for regulatory announcements, useful because Kosovo outlets are individually unreliable in archival persistence.

source_name: Lajmi.net — consumer-finance and banking coverage
why_relevant: Carries consumer-facing banking/credit journalism (mortgage vs rent, lending conditions) that sometimes surfaces bank-conduct issues before they become supervisory matters. Low priority, redundancy only.

source_name: Centralna banka Republike Kosovo (CBK/BQK) — Serbian-language site (?lang=sr)
source_subtype: central bank / regulator official site (language variant)
why_relevant: Primary regulator issuing the cash-operations rules that banned non-euro cash. Under Kosovo's Law on the Use of Languages it publishes Serbian-language versions of regulations, notices and consultation drafts; observed SRB-prefixed regulation PDFs (e.g. wp-content/uploads/.../SRB-7.-Rregullore-per-informacionet-e-transfereve-finale.pdf?lang=sr) confirm a parallel Serbian document track distinct from the Albanian one.

source_name: CBK — Regulation on Cash Operations / plan to facilitate implementation (news + legal framework)
why_relevant: The authoritative text of the measure at the centre of this cell: Regulation on Cash Operations adopted by the CBK Governing Board 27 Dec 2023, in force 1 Feb 2024, plus the transition/deadline plan (three-month facilitation period, mobile banking units, ATM deployment and dinar-euro exchange facilitation in the four northern municipalities). Deadlines and enforcement steps originate here.

source_name: Kosovo Online
why_relevant: Belgrade-aligned Serbian-language portal dedicated to Kosovo, with a dedicated economy section that tracks CBK measures, dinar payment workarounds, pensions/salaries channels and analytic pieces on whether a dinar payment solution can be found. English mirror at /en/.

source_name: Radio Kontakt Plus (Kosovska Mitrovica)
why_relevant: Long-running North Mitrovica Serbian-language broadcaster; carries operational-level detail on banking service availability for Serb clients (e.g. Poštanska štedionica statements on client funds and where services remain available after branch suspensions). Useful for on-the-ground service-continuity signals a regulator feed will never show.

source_name: Narodna banka Srbije (NBS) — statements on Kosovo dinar transport and payments
why_relevant: The counterpart central bank. NBS publishes formal reactions to CBK measures (calling the regulation discriminatory and asking for its withdrawal), plus statements on dinar cash shipments to Kosovo for salaries/pensions/social benefits and on its role as payment-system operator. Essential for the two-regulator picture in Serb-majority municipalities.

source_name: Banka Poštanska štedionica a.d. Beograd
why_relevant: The Serbian state bank that carried the dinar payment channel (salaries, pensions, social transfers) for Kosovo Serbs; its branches in Kosovo were closed by Kosovo Police as unlicensed institutions and it responded by opening mobile/prefabricated units at Jarinje, Brnjak, Merdare and Končulj. Its own client notices are the primary record of how the parallel payment channel was relocated.

source_name: Kancelarija za Kosovo i Metohiju, Vlada Republike Srbije
why_relevant: Serbian government body that funds and coordinates the parallel administrative and payment infrastructure for Serb-majority municipalities; announces measures such as the four prefabricated Poštanska štedionica units near administrative crossings, and reacts to CBK enforcement. Pointer to further Serbian-state actors (Uprava za trezor, PIO fond).

source_name: Kancelarija poverenika za jezike / Office of the Language Commissioner (Kosovo)
why_relevant: Institution that receives and reports complaints about failures to publish official documents in Serbian — directly determines whether a CBK regulation, consultation or deadline is actually available in Serbian and how late. Reported ~40 language-law complaints in 2024. A structural early-warning source for Serbian-language coverage gaps in the regulatory feed itself.

source_name: NGO Aktiv (Severna Mitrovica) — publications archive
why_relevant: The main Kosovo Serb civil-society research organisation, publishing annual analyses of the position of the Serb community including institutional, economic and service-access dimensions; the natural producer of structured, citable analysis of what the dinar/euro rules did to household payments and banking access in Serb-majority municipalities. Also a pointer to further actors and donors (e.g. Norwegian Embassy, Language Commissioner cooperation).

source_name: Radio KIM (Čaglavica/Gračanica)
why_relevant: Serbian-language outlet covering the central-Kosovo Serb enclaves (Gračanica, Priština surroundings) rather than the north — needed because the dinar/payment rules bite differently in enclaves with no Serbian bank presence at all. Complements the north-focused KoSSev/Kontakt Plus.

source_name: Gorazdevac Media Group / Radio Goraždevac
why_relevant: Western-Kosovo (Peć/Metohija) Serbian-language outlet; reported the closure of the Serbian Treasury Administration and five Poštanska štedionica branches in the north, i.e. it carries enforcement events against the parallel financial infrastructure with local specificity.

source_name: Kosinfo — aggregator of Kosovo Serbian-language media
why_relevant: Multi-source aggregator ('više izvora jedna stranica') pulling feeds from Radio Goraždevac, Radio KIM, Gračanica online and other Kosovo Serb outlets — the cheapest single entry point to enumerate and monitor the whole Serbian-language Kosovo media layer, including small outlets not otherwise indexed.

source_name: Radio Slobodna Evropa (RFE/RL) — Balkan service, Kosovo economy coverage
why_relevant: Independent Serbian-language reporting with explanatory depth on the practical consequences of the dinar ban (accounts, salaries, pensions) and on incidents such as the NBS cash vehicle turned back at Jarinje. Higher editorial standard than the aligned Belgrade portals, so it is the best cross-check layer for Kosovo Online/Tanjug claims.

source_name: N1 Srbija — Kosovo/economy desk
why_relevant: Belgrade regional broadcaster that carried both the CBK announcement and the NBS demand that the regulation be withdrawn as discriminatory — i.e. it reliably surfaces the regulator-versus-regulator exchange that defines this cell.

source_name: Danas — ekonomija (Belgrade daily)
why_relevant: Independent Belgrade daily with an economy desk that covers NBS reactions to CBK measures; useful as a non-state Belgrade counterweight to Tanjug/RTS framing.

source_name: Tanjug / RTS — Serbian state media on Kosovo financial institutions
why_relevant: State agency and public broadcaster carry the official Serbian-state version of events affecting banking access in Serb-majority municipalities (branch closures, mobile units, client-funds assurances). Low independent credibility but high value as the authoritative record of what the Serbian state says and does.

source_name: Glas Amerike (VOA) — Serbian service, Kosovo north coverage
why_relevant: Reported the concrete enforcement action — Kosovo Police closing six Poštanska štedionica branches and seizing 74 million dinars — which is exactly the kind of enforcement datapoint (amount, count, municipality) needed to track CBK/state enforcement against non-licensed payment providers.

source_name: Vreme — economy section (Serbian weekly)
why_relevant: Analytical Serbian weekly documenting the persistent gap between the rule and reality ('dinar still in circulation in Serbian municipalities in Kosovo') — valuable for compliance-reality assessment rather than event detection. Has an English mirror.

source_name: Medija centar (Čaglavica) — Kosovo Serb press-release hub
why_relevant: Republishes institutional statements and announcements aimed at the Kosovo Serb community, including CBK currency announcements; functions as a low-cost aggregation point for Serbian-language institutional communications and as a directory of Kosovo Serb media and NGOs.

source_name: UNS — Društvo novinara Kosova i Metohije (DNKiM)
why_relevant: Journalists' association desk documenting whether Kosovo institutions actually deliver documents and regulatory information in Serbian — a direct signal on the availability and lag of Serbian-language regulatory text, and a pointer to Serbian-language Kosovo journalists and outlets.

source_name: Balkan Insight (BIRN) — Kosovo euro-only rule coverage
why_relevant: English-language investigative coverage of how Kosovo intended commercial banks to operationalise the euro-only rule; bridges the Serbian-language reality to an internationally citable record and is useful for validating dates and official positions.

source_name: EEAS / EU Office in Kosovo — Serbian-language statements
why_relevant: The EU repeatedly pressed on the dinar measure's implementation and on bilingualism compliance by Kosovo's administration, publishing statements in Serbian. EU pressure has historically shifted CBK implementation deadlines, so these statements are leading indicators for regulatory timing.

source_name: UN Kosovo Team — Serbian-language press releases
why_relevant: Publishes Serbian-language (SRB-prefixed) press material on language rights and community access to services in Kosovo; a secondary institutional channel where Serbian-language documentation obligations and service-access issues are recorded.
